title: TOGGLE: Temporal Logic-Guided Large Language Model Compression for Edge
problem: Existing LLM compression techniques like quantization and pruning often degrade critical linguistic properties and lack formal guarantees for preserving model behavior during compression, limiting reliable deployment on edge devices.
motivation: Deploying LLMs on resource-constrained edge devices requires compression techniques that preserve linguistic correctness and behavior, not just numerical accuracy.
method: TOGGLE leverages Signal Temporal Logic (STL) to formally specify and enforce linguistic properties during compression. The framework employs STL robustness-guided Bayesian optimization to systematically explore layer-wise quantization and pruning configurations, generating compressed models that formally satisfy specified linguistic constraints without requiring retraining or fine-tuning.
key_novelty: First integration of formal methods (Signal Temporal Logic) into LLM compression, enabling verification that compressed models satisfy formal linguistic property specifications.
contributions: STL-based formal specification framework for linguistic properties in LLM compression
Robustness-guided Bayesian optimization for exploring compression configurations
Compression without retraining or fine-tuning while satisfying formal constraints
Up to 3.3× FLOPs reduction and 68.8% model size reduction on GPT-2, DeepSeek-V2, LLaMA 3, Mistral

metrics.other: 68.8% model size reduction; formal verification guarantees

limitations: Limited to formally specifiable linguistic properties; evaluation only on relatively small LLMs and moderate compression ratios; applicability to larger models (70B+) is not demonstrated.
primary_theme: Formally-verified LLM compression via temporal logic
